claims.text: When choosing between two different avatars for a business offering, focus on the avatar that already has strong earning potential and substantial existing income (employed professionals seeking salary increases) rather than the beginner avatar, because the value delta you can provide is much higher while the delivery cost remains low.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: One avatar is already gainfully employed
claims.mechanism: Professionals with existing income have more earning potential to unlock; the margin between value provided and cost to provide it widens significantly with this avatar, creating better unit economics.
bounded_by: Does not apply when avatars have similar earning potential
Does not apply when cost-to-serve differs dramatically between avatars

claims.text: The core decision framework for selecting an avatar is the value delta versus delivery cost: prioritize opportunities where the gap between the value provided and the cost to provide it is largest.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Multiple business or avatar options exist
Cost and value delivery can be quantified
claims.mechanism: Large value-to-cost ratios create superior unit economics, which compound into scalability and profitability.

claims.text: For outcome-based education offers targeting employed professionals seeking salary increases, a six-month engagement with a guaranteed outcome (e.g., raise achieved or the program is free; customer pays only if they reach the promised outcome) is a defensible offer structure.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Avatar is employed and earning already
Clear, measurable outcome (salary increase) is promised
Engagement duration is 6 months or similar commitment
claims.mechanism: Outcome-based pricing aligns the vendor's incentive with the customer's success, reducing objection-handling friction and increasing conviction.
bounded_by: Requires customer willingness to measurably prove outcome (e.g., offer letter, salary bump evidence)
Does not apply to outcomes that cannot be documented (e.g., subjective skill improvement without income proof)

claims.text: Traffic should be directed to the About/product page rather than a generic lead magnet, because the About page converts higher when it clearly specifies the promised outcome and the exact avatar it targets.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Promised outcome is specific and credible
About page is optimized for avatar clarity
claims.mechanism: Clarity on who you serve and what outcome they get reduces friction for high-fit prospects; lead magnets add an extra step that delays conversion without filtering.
bounded_by: Assumes About page is optimized for outcome clarity (not generic company description)

examples.text: A tech education community ($50/month) targeting both new-to-tech beginners and experienced professionals seeking higher salaries could focus on the experienced professional avatar instead. Experienced professionals already have jobs and earning potential; training them to move into higher-paying roles is a high-value outcome. The vendor provides structured guidance and networking, but the customer's existing income base and job-seeking skills reduce delivery burden on the vendor. The value delta (potential $20k+ annual salary increase) versus delivery cost (curriculum and access) makes this more attractive than building for beginners who may lack the income to pay for premium offers and require more foundational support.

practices.text: Run paid traffic directly to your About page rather than using a lead magnet landing page when your avatar is clearly defined.
